ratings_why.fun: Winding the moon to choose your shop phase and your fight phase is a real decision each turn, and the board grows in readable Full Moon bursts.
ratings_why.distinct: A visible clock you can wind, with a full moon that changes the fight, plays unlike today's tribes; Borrow itself is a familiar copy effect.

verdict_why: v2 closed the unclear cases (Old Wat's resale, Waxwell's stacking, Grandam's copies); what's left is wording polish and UI, not fixes.

points.text: Borrow is readable only if the card face shows the borrowed text and an arrow to its lender while the moon is Full; build that UI before judging the tribe in play.

Grandam of the Forms is the longest card in the tribe. Try: "New Moon: summon a Leveret. Then each Leveret borrowing a Hare becomes a copy of it, keeping its gains. Once a turn." Put the rest in reminder text.

Witch in Borrowed Shape reads "In fights only" and Silverpenny says "whatever the moon's phase", so a player may think the Witch also ignores the moon. "Moonlit, in fights: Borrow the enemy across" shows the Full requirement on the card.
The Moon-Scour should say whether the Full Moon now firing counts ("including this one").

The brief's "stillness then sudden speed" (lying in the form, then bolting) is missing, and Waning is thin. A Waning card that sits still and then bolts, for example attacking first after a Waning shop, would fill both.

standouts.why: Jill Longshanks boxing the enemy across is the March-ring fantasy in one line, and Moonlit making her untouchable is easy to read.
Old Wat, thrown out and back every turn, is the character's joke told by the card's rules.
Dusk Nurse feeding the units behind her, twice when Waning, is the hare mother visiting her leverets at dusk.

weakest.why: Silver Sixpence Doe is a plain gold-on-trigger card; the silver-sixpence lore (witch-hares harmed only by silver) does nothing.
Ring Referee is a generic tribe buff; the referee reading the bout as prophecy is not in the text.
Almanac Jill is a clean turner but the almanac fantasy (knowing the sky) doesn't show in what she does.

flags.note: Created copies that count for triples, fired twice with Dame Waxwell, are the likeliest runaway.
Sister Silverpenny copying another tribe's Tier 6 capstone at Tier 5, always on.
Golden Dame Waxwell with Meikle Care and Ring Referee stacks large Full Moon payouts each turn.
